liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Space** (2 reviews): Space runs about 13 minutes and is jammed out hard with drums; Drums into Space is the low point, with a not particularly inspired Space [13][18]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Franklin's Tower, Peggy-O and Eyes of the World as excellent [20]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Black Peter is played unusually fast, a rare and excellent version [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-09-05.mtx.seamons.ht63.110829.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 166 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd79-09-05.glassberg.unknown.8457.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is pretty good and can sound fine with some equalization [22]
- **gd1979-09-05.156351.senn441.senn421.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 169 min [4]
- **gd1979-09-05.151987.fob.nak700.cm.wagner.miller.t..flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 166 min [7]
- **gd79-09-05.sbd.clugston.9453.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [10]. Said about its sound: Good quality matrix, though audience tape occasionally bleeds in; Patches appear here and there; the start of Half-Step is hard to hear [12][13]

## Around the show

- Crowd was from the New York area; reviewer attended the show after spending the day in the Village [15]
- At the end of Scarlet, about 19,000 fans asked where Donna was [15]
- The Garden crowd went wild during Loser [17]
- Donna was absent, which drew laughter at the end of Scarlet [19]
- WPLJ staff handed out free stickers to fans entering; the radio station then played rock [21]
- Parts of the show are unusually jumpy for fall 1979 [12]
- Scarlet>Fire is the second killer version that year, alongside 1/7/79 [17]
- Strong first set signaled a strong second set; playing tight with hot solos [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-09-05.mtx.seamons.ht63.110829.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16) [1]. Also: Soundboard transferred by Charlie Miller, recorded by Barry Glassberg; Rob Bertrando helped with pitch correction [1]
- **gd79-09-05.glassberg.unknown.8457.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: NAK 700's [3]
- **gd1979-09-05.156351.senn441.senn421.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton for the recording, as well as the transfer and harddrive; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441 (left + right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [4]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton; Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 9-second patch in the Drums > Space transition [4]
- **gd1979-09-05.151987.fob.nak700.cm.wagner.miller.t..flac16**: taped by Recorded by Bob Wagner; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 18, 2021; source: (FOB/11th Row) Nakamichi CM700 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-158SD/Dolby B) [7]. Also: Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 masters from Glassberg; a tape flip in Drums was hidden with a crossfade [7]
- **gd79-09-05.sbd.clugston.9453.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard with aud patches [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.gratefulseconds.com: [Madison Square Garden Took One Million Souls During Grateful Dead's 52-Show 15-Year Run, 1979-1994](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2017/08/madison-square-garden-took-one-million.html) [24]
- Fan art by Today in 1979: [Grateful Dead @ Madison Square Garden](https://todayin1979.weebly.com/blog/grateful-dead-madison-square-garden) [25]
